newsitem.title: FRANCE: Count battles takeover of Chateau d'Yquem vineyard.
newsitem.headline: Count battles takeover of Chateau d'Yquem vineyard.

text.p: Count Alexandre de Lur Saluces pledged on Monday to step up his battle against the takeover of the prestigious Chateau d'Yquem vineyard, which he has managed for years, by French luxury goods group LVMH.
"Contrary to what LVMH announced prematurely on November 28, Yquem has not been purchased by LVMH," the count said in a statement, announcing he would fight the takeover in court.
Yquem makes one of the world's most celebrated and costly wines, a golden-coloured sweet white from France's Sauterne district.
Prices range from 600 francs ($115) for the 1987 vintage, a poor year, to more than 50,000 francs ($10,000) for older vintages.
LVMH had announced last month that it was taking control of the vineyard after striking a deal with most members of a feuding family that has held the property since 1785.
It said it concluded a deal with owners of about 55 percent of the 113-hectare (279 acre) property despite the count's opposition.
LVMH did not say how much it was paying for the controlling stake in Chateau d'Yquem, but an industry expert estimated the value of the entire property at one billion francs.
News of the purchase triggered fierce debate in the wine world over whether LVMH would now preserve the wine's high quality standards or lower them to make the property more profitable.
Count de Lur Saluces said in a statement that under French law, the property could not legally be sold unless both he and his brother Eugene agreed to the transaction.
He said ownership of the legendary vineyard by LVMH was "incompatible with the extraordinary demands required to make this wine of exceptional quality".
